smile.definition: A facial expression characterized by turning up the corners of the mouth.

grin.definition: To draw back the lips and reveal the teeth, in a smile, grimace, or snarl.

beam.definition: To express with a beaming face or smile.

smirk.definition: A smile expressing smugness or scorn instead of pleasure.

laugh.definition: A facial expression characteristic of a person laughing.

wink.definition: A very short time (as the time it takes the eye to blink or the heart to beat).

twinkle.definition: Merriment expressed by a brightness or gleam or animation of countenance.

dimple.definition: A small natural hollow in the cheek or chin.

frown.definition: A facial expression of dislike or displeasure.

pout.definition: To make a sad face and thrust out one's lower lip.

tear.definition: A drop of the clear salty saline solution secreted by the lacrimal glands.

cry.definition: A loud utterance of emotion (especially when inarticulate).

quiver.definition: To shake with fast, tremulous movements.

droop.definition: To droop, sink, or settle from or as if from pressure or loss of tautness.

gloom.definition: A state of partial or total darkness.

glare.definition: A light within the field of vision that is brighter than the brightness to which the eyes are adapted.

clench-jaw.definition: To tighten the jaw muscles or press the teeth together, often because of stress, anger, or determination.
clench-jaw.exampleUsage: He clenched his jaw when he heard the frustrating news.

furrow-brow.definition: To pull the eyebrows together so that lines form on the forehead, often showing worry or concentration.
furrow-brow.exampleUsage: She furrowed her brow while solving the difficult problem.

flare-nostrils.definition: To make the openings of the nose widen, often during anger, strong emotion, or hard breathing.
flare-nostrils.exampleUsage: His nostrils flared as he took a deep breath.

sneer.definition: A facial expression of contempt or scorn.

grit-teeth.definition: To press the teeth tightly together, often because of anger, pain, or determination.
grit-teeth.exampleUsage: She gritted her teeth and finished the difficult climb.

stare.definition: A fixed look with eyes open wide.

squint.definition: Abnormal alignment of one or both eyes.

gasp.definition: A short labored intake of breath with the mouth open.

wide-eyes.definition: Eyes opened more widely than usual, often showing surprise, fear, or strong interest.
wide-eyes.exampleUsage: He stared at the huge building with wide eyes.

dropped-jaw.definition: A mouth and lower jaw that fall open because of strong surprise or shock.
dropped-jaw.exampleUsage: Her dropped jaw showed how surprised she was by the news.

raised-eyebrows.definition: Eyebrows lifted upward, often to show surprise, doubt, interest, or a question.
raised-eyebrows.exampleUsage: His raised eyebrows showed that he was surprised.

pale-face.definition: A face that has lost some of its usual color, often because of fear, illness, or shock.
pale-face.exampleUsage: Her pale face made her friends ask whether she felt well.

tremble.definition: To move or jerk quickly and involuntarily up and down or sideways.

yawn.definition: An involuntary intake of breath through a wide open mouth.

blush.definition: Sudden reddening of the face (as from embarrassment or guilt or shame or modesty).

eye-roll.definition: An upward or circular movement of the eyes used to show annoyance, boredom, or disbelief.
eye-roll.exampleUsage: He gave an eye roll when he heard the same excuse again.

nod.definition: To lower and raise the head, as to indicate assent or agreement or confirmation.

shake-head.definition: To move the head from side to side, often as a facial or body signal of disagreement or disbelief.
shake-head.exampleUsage: She shook her head when she realized the story was not true.
shake-head.arabicTranslation: هزّ الرأس من جانب إلى آخر

bite-lip.definition: To hold or press part of the lip between the teeth, often because of nervousness, worry, or concentration.
bite-lip.exampleUsage: He bit his lip while waiting for the result.

stick-out-tongue.definition: To extend the tongue beyond the lips, sometimes as a playful or rude gesture.
stick-out-tongue.exampleUsage: The child stuck out his tongue playfully for the photo.

raise-hand.definition: To lift one hand, often to ask a question, volunteer, vote, or get attention.
raise-hand.exampleUsage: She raised her hand to answer the teacher's question.

shrug.definition: To raise one's shoulders to indicate indifference or resignation.

thumbs-up.definition: A hand gesture that raises the thumb signals approval, agreement, or praise for someone’s performance.
